title: Not-for-profit Sector Freedom to Advocate Bill 2013

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would prevent Commonwealth agreements with not-for-profit organisations from restricting their advocacy about federal laws, policies or actions, and invalidate clauses imposing such restrictions.
Commonwealth agencies would be barred from including prohibited terms, and affected clauses in existing agreements would become void when the proposed law begins to operate.
The protection would cover releasing information that is not confidential, while excluding personal and confidential information, and would start the day after Royal Assent.
changes: Agencies would be prohibited from putting advocacy restrictions into Commonwealth agreements with covered organisations.
Invalidation would apply to agreements made before commencement as well as later agreements.
Rights and liabilities acquired under prohibited terms before commencement would remain enforceable.
Reasonable compensation would be available for any acquisition of property that otherwise lacked just terms.
summary.affected: Not-for-profit organisations entering Commonwealth agreements and Commonwealth agencies are affected.

speeches.speaker: Mitch Fifield
speeches.brief: Backed the Not-for-profit Sector Freedom to Advocate Bill, arguing not-for-profits, of which there are over 600,000 in Australia, should not be treated as instruments of government, and proposed replacing the Australian Charities and Not-for-profits Commission with a smaller advisory body while protecting the sector's ability to advocate on Commonwealth policy.

speeches.speaker: David Bradbury
speeches.brief: Introduced the Not-for-Profit Sector Freedom to Advocate Bill 2013, which would prohibit and invalidate gag clauses in Commonwealth agreements restricting not-for-profit organisations from advocating on government policy, noting the sector comprises around 600,000 organisations and about eight per cent of national employment.

speeches.speaker: Kevin Andrews
speeches.brief: Supported the Not-for-profit Sector Freedom to Advocate Bill but criticised the government for creating the Australian Charities and Not-for-Profits Commission as an added bureaucratic burden, and pledged a coalition government would transfer its functions to the sector while retaining the common law definition of charity and the public benefit test, consistent with the 2001 charities definition inquiry, the 2008 Henry review and the 2010 Productivity Commission report.

speeches.speaker: David Bradbury
speeches.brief: Defended the Not-for-Profit Sector Freedom to Advocate Bill 2013, accusing Liberal state governments in New South Wales and Queensland of imposing gag clauses on community and legal service organisations, and challenged the Leader of the Opposition to publicly condemn the practice by his state colleagues.
